1. The instant applications have been filed on behalf of the applicants/appellants seeking condonation of delay of 45 days and 67 days respectively in filing and re-filing the captioned appeal.
2. For the sufficient cause being show in the applications, the same are allowed.
Accordingly, the delay of 45 days in filing and 67 days in re-filing the captioned appeal is condoned.
3. The application stands disposed of.
MAC.APP. 276/2024, CM APPL. 31278/2024 (Stay) & CM APPL. 31279/2024 (Exemption from depositing the amount)

sentences.text: 1 (b) Any other or further order, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case may also be passed in favour of the appellants and against the respondents."

2. Heard.
3.
Issue notice.
Notice is accepted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1.

4. In regard to the prayer of the appellants with respect to the interim relief, this Court is of the view that the instant matter requires consideration and, prima facie, the balance of convenience lies in favour of the appellants.

5. Therefore, subject to the deposition of the 50% of the compensation amount awarded by the learned Tribunal, alongwith interest from the date of filing of the claim petition, before the Registrar General of this Court within four weeks from today, the operation of the impugned award dated 22nd September, 2023 shall be kept in abeyance till the next date of hearing.
The amount so deposited by the appellant shall be invested in an interest bearing FDR in an auto renewal mode.
6. On filing PF within a week, issue notice to the respondents No.2 and 3 through all permissible modes, returnable before the Joint Registrar (Judl.) on 20th September, 2024.
CHANDRA DHARI SINGH, J AUGUST 12, 2024 Dy/ryp
